title: Festival appearances, a Boston Common one-shot, and closing the 1950s
summary: He recalls other festivals and a Boston Common concert tape, says anyone who survived the 1950s should be congratulated, and mentions Jazzland recordings.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Just speaking about festivals of the past, it seems like it's countless now, the number of festivals (inaudible) you've been around. And even starting in the '50s, you were pretty active. You were out here, I think, in one memorable one I recall that had Roy Eldridge, Ben Webster, Earl Hines --
Anyway, that was -- you have made appearances by yourself and with your own band, other peoples' bands, just a variety of contexts.

I heard a tape not too long ago that was sent to me by a friend, Joe McDonald in San Francisco, a drummer. He worked with me for a short period of time, and was a good friend of Bill Paul Harris'. And they arranged -- the Arts

or society Society did a think in Boston on the Commons with the local hot players, and I fronted the band and we did some of our charts, and he sent me a tape, and it sounded remarkably good. I was really amazed.
Well, this would be during that '50s period.
Okay, well, if -- do you have anything else to say about that period, the decade of the '50s?
No, but anyone who survived it should be congratulated.
Should be congratulated. You then went through a number of recordings, too. You have one on the Jazzland.
Well, they usually were things that were recorded for some other reason. Someone would --
Nat and Adderly was on it, yeah. In closing the '50s --
